lessons.title: Your first SwiftData model, container, context, query, and CRUD
lessons.summary: Create a real record store, perform explicit save operations, and separate in-memory observation from durable success.
objectives: Construct a SwiftData model, container and context.
Read records with Query and perform explicit CRUD saves.
Handle pending changes, save failure and whole-context rollback honestly.
Separate in-memory fixtures from disk durability and migration evidence.

sections.title: Persistence adds a contract beyond observation
sections.html:
Android Room gives you a familiar reason for a database: records must outlive the screen and process. SwiftData integrates persistence and model observation with SwiftUI, but it is not a one-to-one port of Room annotations or DAO behavior. A model schema, a container, a context and a query each answer a different question. Naming those boundaries makes your first store much easier to debug than treating Model as an all-purpose ViewModel.

This complete source targets a scratch iOS 17+ app using Xcode 15 or later. SwiftData was introduced with iOS 17 and relies on macro-capable tooling. Replace the generated App and root declarations, keeping one entry. No earlier example types are needed. All records are synthetic. This is a first local store, not a migration, cloud synchronization feature, account store or implemented company-client persistence layer.

The app uses a persistent container and explicitly disables autosave for its main context so you can study save outcomes. Its preview uses a fresh in-memory container instead, keeping visual experiments away from the app's disk store. An in-memory fixture can prove CRUD behavior in a test context but cannot prove process-restart durability.

sections.title: Model describes persistent fields and identity
sections.html:
@Model is a macro on a class that generates SwiftData model support. StoredNote has an explicit UUID identity, a title and a creation Date. Attribute's unique option declares uniqueness for the identifier in this local schema. It is not a general authorization mechanism or a promise that every synchronization backend supports that constraint. The lesson does not configure CloudKit.

import Foundation
import SwiftData
import SwiftUI

@Model
final class StoredNote {
    @Attribute(.unique) var id: UUID
    var title: String
    var createdAt: Date

    init(id: UUID = UUID(), title: String, createdAt: Date = Date()) {
        self.id = id
        self.title = title
        self.createdAt = createdAt
    }
}

struct StoredNoteRow: View {
    @Bindable var note: StoredNote
    var body: some View {
        TextField("Synthetic title", text: $note.title)
    }
}

@MainActor
struct StoreScreen: View {
    @Environment(\.modelContext) private var context
    @Query(sort: \StoredNote.createdAt) private var notes: [StoredNote]
    @State private var newTitle = ""
    @State private var status = "Edit, then explicitly save"

    var body: some View {
        NavigationStack {
            List {
                Section("Add") {
                    TextField("New synthetic title", text: $newTitle)
                    Button("Add and save") {
                        let title = newTitle.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
                        guard !title.isEmpty else { return }
                        context.insert(StoredNote(title: title))
                        newTitle = ""
                        save()
                    }
                    .disabled(newTitle.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty)
                }
                Section("Stored and pending notes") {
                    ForEach(notes) { note in StoredNoteRow(note: note) }
                        .onDelete { offsets in
                            let snapshot = notes
                            for offset in offsets where snapshot.indices.contains(offset) {
                                context.delete(snapshot[offset])
                            }
                            save()
                        }
                }
                Section {
                    Button("Save pending changes") { save() }
                    Button("Discard ALL pending changes", role: .destructive) {
                        context.rollback()
                        status = "Pending changes discarded"
                    }
                    Text(status)
                }
            }
            .navigationTitle("Synthetic store")
            .toolbar { EditButton() }
        }
    }

    private func save() {
        do {
            try context.save()
            status = "Save succeeded"
        } catch {
            status = "Save failed; changes are still pending. Retry or discard."
        }
    }
}

@main
@MainActor
struct StoreLessonApp: App {
    private let container: ModelContainer?
    private let setupFailed: Bool

    init() {
        do {
            let value = try ModelContainer(for: StoredNote.self)
            value.mainContext.autosaveEnabled = false
            container = value
            setupFailed = false
        } catch {
            container = nil
            setupFailed = true
        }
    }

    var body: some Scene {
        WindowGroup {
            if let container {
                StoreScreen().modelContainer(container)
            } else {
                Text(setupFailed ? "Store setup failed; no data was deleted."
                                : "Store unavailable")
                    .padding()
            }
        }
    }
}

@MainActor
struct MemoryStorePreview: View {
    private let container: ModelContainer?
    init() {
        do {
            let config = ModelConfiguration(isStoredInMemoryOnly: true)
            let value = try ModelContainer(for: StoredNote.self, configurations: config)
            value.mainContext.autosaveEnabled = false
            value.mainContext.insert(StoredNote(title: "Demo fixture"))
            try value.mainContext.save()
            container = value
        } catch {
            container = nil
        }
    }

    var body: some View {
        if let container {
            StoreScreen().modelContainer(container)
        } else {
            Text("In-memory fixture setup failed")
        }
    }
}

#Preview("Fresh in-memory store") {
    MemoryStorePreview()
}

The initializer fills every stored field and supplies default values for a new synthetic record. The UUID is created once for that construction. Editing a title does not generate a new record ID. The query orders by createdAt using a key path; if two records have equal timestamps, a product requiring deterministic tie order should add an appropriate secondary sort rule. Do not use changing array positions as identity.

ModelContainer holds schema and storage configuration. ModelContext tracks fetched models and pending changes, and saves them to the container's store. Query supplies view data from the installed context and responds to relevant changes. Bindable exposes controls for the model's editable title. These are related integrations, but an updated query display is not evidence that disk saving succeeded.

sections.title: Install the container before asking for a context
sections.html:
The app constructs ModelContainer once at its app boundary and installs it with modelContainer on StoreScreen. That modifier supplies the context environment required by the screen and Query. Constructing a component directly in a preview without this dependency can fail or use an unintended setup. The in-memory host supplies its own container, schema and fixture insert/save explicitly.

Container construction can throw. The app catches setup failure and displays a recovery message without deleting any store. A production app needs a more useful diagnostic and recovery policy, but automatically erasing persisted data to make startup pass would be a destructive change outside this lesson. Do not replace every try with try! to hide the difference between a compile-time declaration and a fallible store operation.

MainContext is intended for the main-actor UI context in this example. Do not send its managed model objects into arbitrary background tasks or share the same context across isolation boundaries. Use an appropriate separate context or model-actor design for larger asynchronous work and transfer safe identifiers or values. Existing persistence deep dives cover those boundaries; the first CRUD app deliberately stays within one UI context.

sections.title: Insert, read, update and delete with explicit save
sections.html:
Add and save trims the creation draft, guards against empty input, inserts a new model into the context, clears the input and then attempts save. Query may show that new pending model before save succeeds. The status says whether the save completed, so the screen does not equate visible insertion with durable success. On failure, changes remain pending in this teaching policy and Save pending changes provides a retry path.

Reading is Query's sorted notes array. Updating happens through StoredNoteRow's Bindable TextField and requires Save pending changes for an explicit durable commit because autosave is disabled. Those title edits are live in the context, not staged per-row transactions. Deletion maps the unfiltered displayed offsets to a snapshot of current model objects, marks those objects for deletion and attempts save. If search is later added, map through visible IDs as in lesson 077.

A context save can include all its pending changes, not just the one row whose button was pressed. That matters when several editors share it. This beginner screen exposes one small context and explicitly labels pending changes. For independently cancellable editors, stage input or isolate the transaction scope instead of assuming each TextField is a separate database transaction.

sections.title: Pending UI and durable storage can disagree
sections.html:
The failed-save status tells the truth: the display can reflect unsaved inserts, edits or deletes. Retry attempts the same pending state; rollback discards all pending changes in this context. The destructive discard button is clearly labeled with that whole-context scope. Do not use rollback as an invisible per-row undo when another editor has unsaved changes in the same context.

Autosave is a separate policy that may be appropriate for another application, but it should not replace understanding fallible saves and transaction ownership. Our explicit-save baseline makes the distinction observable. A successful save supports a local persistence claim under that container; a restart experiment must still verify the actual store location and the launched product. Preview saving to memory does not create durable evidence.

Schema changes, relationships, migrations, uniqueness conflicts, multiple accounts and store protection require additional design. Do not change fields in a deployed store and assume every existing record migrates safely. No such migration is performed here. The repository has its own persistence architecture; this first SwiftData example teaches an adjacent API without claiming the client already uses it.

sections.title: Verify CRUD, retry and restart at separate layers
sections.html:
In the in-memory fixture, add a note, edit a title, explicitly save, fetch through Query, delete and save again. For tests, fetch through a new context in the same container after save to reduce dependence on one context's pending view. A disk-backed restart check uses the launched app, preserves its sandbox and confirms the saved record after relaunch. Clearing the app's data would invalidate that durability experiment.

Exercise Discard with an unsaved title edit and observe the model reverting, then explain its whole-context effect. To test failure, inject or configure a bounded failure fixture and record its actual cause; don't claim that every constraint violation always throws in the same way. The lesson supplies the failure-handling path but does not fabricate a failed disk write.

The verified address model anchor demonstrates an observable in-memory model and a computed currentAddress projection. That is a useful contrast: its annotation is Observable, not Model, and the read-only source does not establish a SwiftData store. The native companion's persistence implementation and build evidence belong to its author. Your handoff should label this snippet as conceptual/type-checked as actually verified, and reserve app-run, restart and migration claims for executed checks.

quiz.question: Query shows a newly inserted model. What does that prove?
options: The context/query can show pending data; durable save still needs evidence
quiz.explanation: Visible observation and persistent commit are different.

quiz.question: What does this rollback action affect?
options: All pending changes in this context
quiz.explanation: Its scope is the context, so unrelated unsaved editors can be affected.

quiz.question: Why use an in-memory preview container?
options: It isolates synthetic preview records from the disk store
quiz.explanation: An in-memory save is not durability evidence.

exercise.brief: Perform first SwiftData CRUD and report pending changes separately from durable results.
steps: Use the complete source in the scratch iOS 17+ target.
Inspect the in-memory preview and its explicit container injection.
Add, edit, Save pending changes, delete and save synthetic notes.
Try an unsaved edit then Discard, naming the whole-context scope.
If you run a disk restart check, record the product/sandbox and actual result; otherwise leave durability pending.
acceptance: The schema, container, context and query roles are explained separately.
Creation rejects blank trimmed input.
Updates require explicit save under the disabled-autosave policy.
Save failure does not claim success or erase the store.
In-memory CRUD, disk restart and migration evidence are not conflated.
exercise.solution:
The CRUD path is model construction → context.insert → context.save, Query for reads, binding mutation → explicit save for updates, and context.delete → save for removal. Before save, Query may reflect tracked changes. Save succeeded means this context's pending changes were committed by its container; Save failed leaves them pending under the stated policy. Rollback discards the full pending context state.

For a meaningful store check, save the fixture, create another ModelContext from the same container and fetch StoredNote with FetchDescriptor. Verify the expected title and ID there, then delete and save and confirm absence through a fresh fetch. That is stronger than looking at the existing row alone, but an in-memory container still cannot prove restart durability. Perform the disk check separately if available, without clearing data. The preview's host constructs a fresh memory store each time, and setup failure shows a message rather than deleting data. No migration, cloud synchronization or company store modification is included in this worked answer.

lessons.title: Capstone: test and debug a complete synthetic feature
lessons.summary: Assemble a shared draft, picker, review and async fixture, then verify behavior with deterministic tests and an honest handoff.
objectives: Assemble a complete synthetic SwiftUI workflow.
Test eligibility, cancellation outcomes and stale-result rejection.
Place source and tests in the correct products.
Write a handoff distinguishing authored examples from executed evidence.

sections.title: Finish one feature with evidence, not just a screen
sections.html:
An experienced Android engineer knows that a feature includes state, user outcomes, tests and debugging evidence. The beginner iOS capstone now combines the preceding skills into one small synthetic plan app. It has a display name, optional topic, reminder, modal picker, Review destination, Reset and an asynchronous suggestion. This is a first end-to-end workflow, not appointment booking or a production client migration.

The complete app source targets iOS 17+ with Xcode 15 or later. Create a scratch iOS App product named SwiftUICapstone and use that Swift module name for the supplied unit-test import. Replace the generated entry/root types with the app source, keeping one entry. Include a unit-test target and a UI-test target through the template or Xcode's Add Target workflow. App source belongs only to the app target; the test declarations belong only to their respective test targets.

The contract is explicit: whitespace-only names cannot Review; choosing a topic commits it; Cancel preserves the previous topic; returning from Review preserves root edits; Reset clears draft fields; only the latest name request can publish suggestion or error. The reminder is synthetic and schedules nothing. No persistence is included in this app; apply lesson 083's store only as a separately scoped extension.

sections.title: A complete root owns the draft and its fixture
sections.html:
PlanDraft is a MainActor observable reference model owned by root State. TopicPicker receives the same reference and commits only when a topic button is activated. Its Cancel merely dismisses. Review reads the same draft, so a return does not require copying values back. LocalSuggestion is an injected synthetic service; its protocol describes one async throwing operation. any Suggesting stores a conforming service behind that contract.

import Foundation
import Observation
import SwiftUI

enum PracticeTopic: String, CaseIterable, Identifiable {
    case reading = "Demo reading"
    case exercises = "Demo exercises"
    var id: Self { self }
}

@MainActor
protocol Suggesting {
    func suggestion(for name: String) async throws -> String
}

@MainActor
struct LocalSuggestion: Suggesting {
    func suggestion(for name: String) async throws -> String {
        try await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(200))
        return "Synthetic suggestion for \(name)"
    }
}

@MainActor
@Observable
final class PlanDraft {
    var name = "" {
        didSet { if name != oldValue { invalidate() } }
    }
    var topic: PracticeTopic?
    var reminder = false
    private(set) var token = UUID()
    private(set) var suggestion = ""
    private(set) var errorMessage: String?

    var canReview: Bool {
        !name.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty && topic != nil
    }

    func invalidate() {
        token = UUID()
        suggestion = ""
        errorMessage = nil
    }

    func reset() {
        name = ""
        topic = nil
        reminder = false
        invalidate()
    }

    func load(service: any Suggesting) async {
        let expected = token
        let input = name
        guard !input.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty else {
            return
        }
        do {
            let value = try await service.suggestion(for: input)
            guard token == expected, !Task.isCancelled else { return }
            suggestion = value
            errorMessage = nil
        } catch {
            guard token == expected, !Task.isCancelled else { return }
            suggestion = ""
            errorMessage = "Synthetic suggestion failed"
        }
    }
}

@MainActor
struct TopicPicker: View {
    @Environment(\.dismiss) private var dismiss
    let draft: PlanDraft

    var body: some View {
        NavigationStack {
            List(PracticeTopic.allCases) { topic in
                Button(topic.rawValue) {
                    draft.topic = topic
                    dismiss()
                }
            }
            .navigationTitle("Choose demo topic")
            .toolbar {
                ToolbarItem(placement: .cancellationAction) {
                    Button("Cancel") { dismiss() }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

@MainActor
struct PlanRoot: View {
    @State private var draft = PlanDraft()
    @State private var showTopics = false
    let service: any Suggesting

    var body: some View {
        @Bindable var editable = draft
        NavigationStack {
            Form {
                TextField("Demo name", text: $editable.name)
                    .accessibilityIdentifier("nameField")
                Toggle("Demo reminder", isOn: $editable.reminder)
                Button(draft.topic?.rawValue ?? "Choose topic") { showTopics = true }
                NavigationLink {
                    VStack(spacing: 16) {
                        Text(draft.name)
                        Text(draft.topic?.rawValue ?? "No topic")
                        Text(draft.suggestion)
                    }
                    .padding()
                    .navigationTitle("Review")
                } label: {
                    Text("Review")
                }
                .disabled(!draft.canReview)
                .accessibilityIdentifier("reviewLink")
                Text(draft.suggestion)
                if let message = draft.errorMessage { Text(message) }
                Button("Reset") { draft.reset() }
                    .accessibilityIdentifier("resetButton")
            }
            .navigationTitle("Synthetic plan")
            .sheet(isPresented: $showTopics) { TopicPicker(draft: draft) }
        }
        .task(id: draft.token) { await draft.load(service: service) }
        .onDisappear { draft.invalidate() }
    }
}

@main
@MainActor
struct SwiftUICapstone: App {
    var body: some Scene {
        WindowGroup { PlanRoot(service: LocalSuggestion()) }
    }
}

#Preview("Local fixture") {
    PlanRoot(service: LocalSuggestion())
}

Name changes revoke the previous token synchronously. The task awaits the model operation directly, while both success and catch branches check current token and cancellation before publishing. Reset invalidates even when name was already empty, so an older request cannot regain authority. These checks are independent of whether the fixture cooperates with cancellation.

The preview supplies the local fixture explicitly and never constructs a production client. It uses a small delay to make interaction observable, not to coordinate tests. The App's module name is a target/product setup detail: if you choose another module, change the test import accordingly. A visible file with the wrong membership cannot satisfy the testing contract.

sections.title: Test invariants and controlled completion order
sections.html:
The following belongs to an iOS 17+ unit-test target whose host is the scratch app, not to the app entry source. XCTest runs assertions against the model. The first test checks meaningful eligibility and Reset. The second uses start expectations and retained continuations to release A1, B and A2 in an adversarial order. It exercises old success and old error publication, including the A → B → A case where text comparison alone would fail.

import XCTest
@testable import SwiftUICapstone

@MainActor
final class ControlledSuggestion: Suggesting {
    private var nextID = 0
    private var pending: [Int: CheckedContinuation<String, Error>] = [:]
    var onStart: ((Int) -> Void)?

    func suggestion(for name: String) async throws -> String {
        let id = nextID
        nextID += 1
        return try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { continuation in
            pending[id] = continuation
            onStart?(id)
        }
    }

    func finish(_ id: Int, with result: Result<String, Error>) {
        guard let continuation = pending.removeValue(forKey: id) else {
            XCTFail("Missing or already finished request")
            return
        }
        continuation.resume(with: result)
    }
}

enum TestFailure: Error { case synthetic }

final class PlanDraftTests: XCTestCase {
    @MainActor
    func testEligibilityAndReset() {
        let draft = PlanDraft()
        draft.name = "   "
        draft.topic = .reading
        XCTAssertFalse(draft.canReview)
        draft.name = "Demo Ada"
        draft.reminder = true
        XCTAssertTrue(draft.canReview)
        draft.reset()
        XCTAssertEqual(draft.name, "")
        XCTAssertNil(draft.topic)
        XCTAssertFalse(draft.reminder)
        XCTAssertFalse(draft.canReview)
    }

    @MainActor
    func testOldSuccessAndErrorCannotReplaceNewA() async {
        let draft = PlanDraft()
        let service = ControlledSuggestion()
        let started0 = expectation(description: "A1 started")
        let started1 = expectation(description: "B started")
        let started2 = expectation(description: "A2 started")
        service.onStart = { id in
            switch id {
            case 0: started0.fulfill()
            case 1: started1.fulfill()
            case 2: started2.fulfill()
            default: XCTFail("Unexpected extra request")
            }
        }

        draft.name = "A"
        let a1 = Task { await draft.load(service: service) }
        await fulfillment(of: [started0], timeout: 2)
        draft.name = "B"
        let b = Task { await draft.load(service: service) }
        await fulfillment(of: [started1], timeout: 2)
        draft.name = "A"
        let a2 = Task { await draft.load(service: service) }
        await fulfillment(of: [started2], timeout: 2)

        service.finish(2, with: .success("Current A2"))
        await a2.value
        XCTAssertEqual(draft.suggestion, "Current A2")
        service.finish(0, with: .success("Old A1"))
        await a1.value
        XCTAssertEqual(draft.suggestion, "Current A2")
        service.finish(1, with: .failure(TestFailure.synthetic))
        await b.value
        XCTAssertEqual(draft.suggestion, "Current A2")
        XCTAssertNil(draft.errorMessage)
    }
}

ControlledSuggestion intentionally does not observe cancellation while waiting. That lets the test challenge freshness even when obsolete work finishes. Each started request is released and each Task is awaited on the normal test path, preventing unfinished continuations from being mistaken for cancelled producers. A robust test harness should additionally drain pending requests on unexpected setup failure or timeout. The two-second expectation timeout is a failure bound, not the schedule used to decide completion order.

These tests are authored examples, not a claim they ran. Use Product → Test with the app scheme's test action and a compatible simulator. Record failures, toolchain and destination. Add a separate invalidation-only test and old-error-for-A1 variation when extending the suite. Do not add tests merely counting body evaluations; test the behavior the user relies on.

sections.title: Test interaction separately from model truth
sections.html:
The following belongs to the UI-test target. It launches the scratch app, types a synthetic name, selects a topic, opens Review, returns and resets. waitForExistence waits for a UI condition rather than assuming a fixed delay. Accessibility identifiers locate stable controls, while labels used for topic choices are fixture strings. A localized suite should use stable identifiers for those choices too.

import XCTest

final class PlanFlowUITests: XCTestCase {
    func testChooseReviewReturnAndReset() {
        let app = XCUIApplication()
        app.launch()
        let name = app.textFields["nameField"]
        XCTAssertTrue(name.waitForExistence(timeout: 5))
        name.tap()
        name.typeText("Demo Ada")
        app.buttons["Choose topic"].tap()
        app.buttons["Demo reading"].tap()
        app.buttons["reviewLink"].tap()
        XCTAssertTrue(app.navigationBars["Review"].waitForExistence(timeout: 5))
        app.navigationBars["Review"].buttons.element(boundBy: 0).tap()
        app.buttons["resetButton"].tap()
        XCTAssertEqual(name.value as? String, "Demo name")
        XCTAssertFalse(app.buttons["reviewLink"].isEnabled)
    }
}

The sample's back-button lookup and empty-field placeholder expectation reflect a simple English simulator fixture. Inspect the actual accessibility hierarchy and adjust those queries for the chosen runtime; do not report a passing UI test just because the source compiles. Model tests cannot prove tap routing, keyboard obstruction, modal gesture behavior or VoiceOver order. UI automation also does not replace assistive-technology inspection and adaptive layout checks.

Add a manual Cancel sequence with an existing topic and verify preservation. Test a long name, large text and a narrow window. For work lifetime, leave the relevant root scope during a controlled request and distinguish task cancellation from publication rejection. Never use real personal data to make the app look realistic.

sections.title: Classify failures by their responsible boundary
sections.html:
If typing does not change eligibility, inspect binding, shared reference and derived reads. If Cancel clears topic, inspect the picker action rather than navigation. If Review is disabled after valid input, check both trimmed name and optional topic. If Reset leaves an old suggestion, inspect invalidation and both completion paths. If old errors overwrite current data, reproduce the gated schedule before changing timing.

If tests cannot import the app, check the Swift module name, test host and membership. A unit-test file compiled into the app target cannot simply import XCTest and become a test bundle. If UI queries fail, inspect runtime accessibility identifiers and hierarchy. If a preview fails, verify its explicit dependencies and compile diagnostics before assuming the app cannot launch.

The active booking demo's project manifest declares separate app, unit-test and UI-test targets, providing verified evidence for those distinct products. Its dependencies and deployment minimum are checkout facts, not requirements to copy into SwiftUICapstone. The company client remains read-only. The companion at labs/SwiftUIWorkbench provides an isolated app and widget target with inspectable source. Check its README and actual target membership before using a component in the capstone.

sections.title: Report what was authored, checked, and observed
sections.html:
Your handoff should include the behavior contract, owner map, fixture description, chosen deployment minimum, module/test membership and exact verification results. Distinguish schema or source review, compiler type checking, linked app build, simulator Run, executed unit tests, executed UI tests, manual accessibility inspection and disk restart. An unperformed check remains pending; it does not become success because a similar repository test exists.

For this capstone, the ownership map is root → one draft; picker and review → that reference; root-associated task → injected suggestion service; token → permission to publish; no store → no process-restart draft. It is intentionally bounded so the learner can explain every boundary. Advanced coordinators, bridge integration, migration and production service adapters remain the earlier core and deeper tracks.

Finish by identifying one failure you reproduced or one check still unperformed, the evidence needed next and the smallest responsible change. That makes the work useful for review and continued learning. Course attendance and a working synthetic feature do not certify exhaustive platform expertise. A clear, tested behavior contract is a practical first iOS delivery milestone.

exercise.solution:
The app and tests above form the worked reference. Start with eligibility/Reset, then run the completion-gated test: A2 publishes Current A2, old A1 success is ignored, and old B error cannot replace it. The token is independent of query text and the fixture intentionally ignores cancellation. Extend that test with explicit invalidation before any replacement request and with old A1 error to challenge the remaining schedules.

The UI sequence should end with an empty name and disabled Review under the supplied English fixture, but query details must match the actual runtime hierarchy. Cancel with an existing topic must preserve it because no cancel action assigns topic. A final note should list actual test command/action, destination, outcome and unresolved failures. If only source type checking was possible, state that; linking, Run and interaction remain pending. No persisted draft, company source change or real request is part of this capstone. Compare with the SwiftUIWorkbench companion using its actual source and recorded verification; a build result does not establish app interaction.
